name: Saint Rita of Cascia
briefBio: Rita was an Italian wife, mother, widow, and Augustinian nun whose life became associated with patience, forgiveness, and prayer through family suffering and religious life. Her devotion to Christ's Passion made her one of the Church's most loved saints of perseverance.

name: Saint Bede the Venerable
briefBio: Bede was an English Benedictine monk, priest, theologian, and historian. His careful biblical commentaries and his Ecclesiastical History of the English People made him one of the great teachers of the early medieval Church.

name: Saint Gregory VII
briefBio: Gregory VII was pope from 1073 to 1085 and a central figure in the Gregorian Reform. He defended the freedom of the Church from secular control and is remembered for his courage during the Investiture Controversy.

name: Saint Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi
briefBio: Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi was a Carmelite nun from Florence known for intense prayer, mystical experiences, and a disciplined love for renewal in the Church. Her writings and witness emphasize charity, humility, and union with Christ.

name: Saint Augustine of Canterbury
briefBio: Augustine was a monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to evangelize the Anglo-Saxons. He became the first Archbishop of Canterbury and laid enduring foundations for Christianity in England.

name: Saint Paul VI
briefBio: Paul VI guided the later sessions of the Second Vatican Council and oversaw its early implementation. His pontificate emphasized evangelization, peace, dialogue, and fidelity to the Church's teaching.

name: Saint Norbert of Xanten
briefBio: Norbert was a reforming bishop and founder of the Premonstratensians. After a deep conversion, he became a preacher of renewal, reverence for the Eucharist, and reconciliation.

name: Saint Ephrem the Syrian
briefBio: Ephrem was a deacon, theologian, hymn writer, and Doctor of the Church. His poetry and hymns taught the faith with unusual beauty and earned him the title Harp of the Holy Spirit.

name: Saint Patrick
briefBio: Patrick was a missionary bishop whose preaching helped establish Christianity in Ireland. His Confession presents a humble, prayerful servant shaped by captivity, conversion, and mission.

name: Saint Josephine Bakhita
briefBio: Josephine Bakhita was kidnapped and enslaved as a child in Sudan before finding freedom and becoming a Canossian sister in Italy. Her life witnesses to forgiveness, dignity, and hope after profound suffering.

name: Saint Blaise
briefBio: Blaise was a bishop and martyr of Sebaste. Devotion to him is especially tied to the blessing of throats, recalling the tradition that he healed a child choking on a fish bone.

name: Saint Angela Merici
briefBio: Angela Merici founded the Company of Saint Ursula, a new form of consecrated life dedicated especially to the education and formation of girls. Her work shaped the later Ursuline tradition.

name: Saint John of God
briefBio: John of God served the poor and sick in Granada with radical charity. His work inspired the Brothers Hospitallers and made him a model of practical mercy.

name: Saint Maria Goretti
briefBio: Maria Goretti was an Italian girl who died after resisting assault and forgiving her attacker. Her witness is often remembered as a sign of purity, mercy, and Christian forgiveness.

name: Saint Teresa of Calcutta
briefBio: Teresa of Calcutta founded the Missionaries of Charity and served the poorest and most abandoned with direct, personal care. Her life made the works of mercy visible to the modern world.

name: Saint Faustina Kowalska
briefBio: Faustina Kowalska was a Polish sister whose diary helped spread devotion to Divine Mercy. Her message centers on trust in Jesus and mercy toward others.

name: Saint John Paul II
briefBio: John Paul II served as pope from 1978 to 2005. His long pontificate emphasized human dignity, evangelization, the family, and the call to holiness in ordinary life.

name: Saint Martin de Porres
briefBio: Martin de Porres was a Dominican lay brother in Lima known for humility, healing care, and love for the poor. His holiness crossed the social and racial barriers of his time.

name: Saint Nicholas
briefBio: Nicholas was bishop of Myra and became famous for generosity, defense of the vulnerable, and pastoral care. Many later traditions about gift-giving grew from devotion to him.

name: Saint Thomas Becket
briefBio: Thomas Becket was Archbishop of Canterbury and a martyr for the freedom of the Church. His conflict with King Henry II ended with his murder in Canterbury Cathedral.
